title: DAS and doubleDAS User Guide
text: following doubleDAS parameters define population, auxiliary varaibles, number sample points draw population, mixing parameter maximum number candidate samples.
code: set.seed(2026)  # Numeric matrix of population coordinates, one unit per row. # x points uniformly in [0,1)^2 myPop <- matrix(runif(2000 * 2), ncol = 2)  # Numeric matrix of auxiliary variables, one row per unit. myAux <- matrix(runif(2000 * 2), ncol = 2) myAux <- myAux / sqrt(rowSums(myAux^2))   # The number of sample points to draw from the population. n <- 150  # Mix in [0, 1]. Default 0.5. alpha <- 0.5  # Maximum number of candidate samples, \code{2 <= J1 <= floor(N/2)}. # Default is \code{min(200, floor(N/2))}. Values above 500 are allowed but # trigger a warning (large assignment problems dominate run time). J1 <- 200

title: Dynamic Assignment Sampling
text: DAS() returns matrix: row candidate sample size n (1-based population indices). first k columns row size-k DAS sample. Doubly balanced samples (MATLAB doubleDAS) mix spatial spread balance auxiliary variables:
code: library(spbalDAS) set.seed(511) pop <- matrix(runif(400), ncol = 2) samp <- DAS(pop, n = 25)          # J1 defaults to min(200, N/2) samp[1, ]                         # one candidate sample of size 25 aux <- cbind(pop, runif(nrow(pop))) dsamp <- doubleDAS(pop, aux, n = 25, alpha = 0.5) # alpha = 1  -> spatially balanced (same objective as DAS) # alpha = 0  -> approximately balanced on aux

what: Doubly balanced Dynamic Assignment Sampling (doubleDAS). — doubleDAS
title: Doubly balanced Dynamic Assignment Sampling (doubleDAS). — doubleDAS
text: Port MATLAB doubleDAS sampler. Candidate samples grow successive linear assignment cost $$C = \alpha\,SB + (1-\alpha)\,B$$ \(SB\) inverse-distance spread used DAS (MATLAB SBMoranIvec) \(B\) squared sum auxiliary variables appending candidate unit (MATLAB LinearAssignment). alpha = 1 spatially balanced (objective DAS). alpha = 0 approximately balanced aux. Values doubly balanced. Reuses arma_dist_al weights, DAS candidate-growth schedule, native_lapjv (Jonker-Volgenant) place MATLAB matchpairs.

J1 Maximum number candidate samples, 2 <= J1 <= floor(N/2). Default min(500, floor(N/2)), matching MATLAB. n_threads Threads cost-matrix fill. See DAS. verbose Print step timings. Default FALSE. cache_W Cache \(N \times N\) inverse-distance matrix alpha > 0. Default N <= 2500. large N usually slower --fly distances.
